The Euler–Mascheroni Constant

Two quantities both diverge, yet the gap between them settles at one value. That gap is the Euler–Mascheroni constant.

The harmonic numbers and the logarithm both grow without end. Still, the space between them narrows and comes to a stop. The gap stops because its increments form a convergent series. That secret is the second formula below.

For example, two 🧑 friends run side by side. Both run endlessly far, but the distance between them stops growing at about 5 meters. That settled distance plays the role of this constant.

γ=lim⁡n→∞(Hn−ln⁡n)≈0.5772\gamma = \lim_{n\to\infty}(H_n - \ln n) \approx 0.5772γ=n→∞lim​(Hn​−lnn)≈0.5772
γ=∑n≥1(1n−ln⁡ ⁣(1+1n))\gamma = \sum_{n\ge1}\left(\frac1n - \ln\!\left(1+\frac1n\right)\right)γ=n≥1∑​(n1​−ln(1+n1​))

By the left half of the hint inequality, ln⁡(n+1)−ln⁡n>1n+1\ln(n+1) - \ln n > \frac{1}{n+1}ln(n+1)−lnn>n+11​, so this difference is negative: γn\gamma_nγn​ is strictly decreasing.

The lower bound appears by splitting ln⁡n\ln nlnn: γn=Hn−∑k=1n−1(ln⁡(k+1)−ln⁡k)=1n+∑k=1n−1(1k−ln⁡(1+1k))\gamma_n = H_n - \sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(\ln(k+1) - \ln k) = \frac{1}{n} + \sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\left(\frac{1}{k} - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)\right)γn​=Hn​−∑k=1n−1​(ln(k+1)−lnk)=n1​+∑k=1n−1​(k1​−ln(1+k1​)), and each bracket is positive by the right half of the hint inequality, ln⁡(1+1k)<1k\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right) < \frac{1}{k}ln(1+k1​)<k1​. Hence γn>1n>0\gamma_n > \frac{1}{n} > 0γn​>n1​>0.

Show that ∑n=1∞(1n−ln⁡(1+1n))=γ\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{n} - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)\right) = \gamma∑n=1∞​(n1​−ln(1+n1​))=γ (a telescoping sum).

∑k=1n(1k−ln⁡(1+1k))=Hn−ln⁡(n+1)=γn−ln⁡(1+1n)\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{k} - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)\right) = H_n - \ln(n+1) = \gamma_n - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)k=1∑n​(k1​−ln(1+k1​))=Hn​−ln(n+1)=γn​−ln(1+n1​)
Show proof

  1. Expanding the partial sum, ∑k=1nln⁡(1+1k)=∑k=1n(ln⁡(k+1)−ln⁡k)=ln⁡(n+1)\sum_{k=1}^{n} \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right) = \sum_{k=1}^{n}(\ln(k+1) - \ln k) = \ln(n+1)∑k=1n​ln(1+k1​)=∑k=1n​(ln(k+1)−lnk)=ln(n+1) telescopes, so ∑k=1n(1k−ln⁡(1+1k))=Hn−ln⁡(n+1)\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\frac{1}{k} - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)\right) = H_n - \ln(n+1)∑k=1n​(k1​−ln(1+k1​))=Hn​−ln(n+1).

  2. Since Hn−ln⁡(n+1)=γn−ln⁡(1+1n)H_n - \ln(n+1) = \gamma_n - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)Hn​−ln(n+1)=γn​−ln(1+n1​), with γn→γ\gamma_n \to \gammaγn​→γ (problem 1) and ln⁡(1+1n)→0\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right) \to 0ln(1+n1​)→0, the partial sums converge to γ\gammaγ. Hence the series sums to γ\gammaγ.

  3. Each term dk:=1k−ln⁡(1+1k)d_k := \frac{1}{k} - \ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)dk​:=k1​−ln(1+k1​) is positive by ln⁡(1+1k)<1k\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right) < \frac{1}{k}ln(1+k1​)<k1​, so this says a series of positive terms sums to γ\gammaγ — this is exactly why the gap between the diverging harmonic series and ln⁡n\ln nlnn converges: the total of these differences is finite.

Numerical check (n=100n = 100n=100): H100−ln⁡101≈5.187377518−4.615120517=0.5722570008H_{100} - \ln 101 \approx 5.187377518 - 4.615120517 = 0.5722570008H100​−ln101≈5.187377518−4.615120517=0.5722570008 — matching the caption and approaching γ≈0.5772\gamma \approx 0.5772γ≈0.5772 (the gap ≈0.005\approx 0.005≈0.005 is the tail ∑k>100dk\sum_{k>100} d_k∑k>100​dk​).
